title: Foundations: say who, what and how
summary: The three parts of almost every good prompt: a role, a task and the context.

lessons.title: Why vague prompts fail
lessons.body: A model fills gaps with guesses. 'Summarise this' leaves out who it is for, how long, and what you need it for. Every gap you close is one less guess.

lessons.title: Role, task, context
lessons.body: Role: who the model should act as. Task: the one thing to do. Context: the facts it cannot know, such as your course, level or deadline. Start with these three before anything else.

exercises.title: Summarise a reading
exercises.scenario: You have a 6-page journal article and 30 minutes before a seminar. 'Summarise this paper.' is too thin.
exercises.task: Rewrite the prompt so you get something you can use in the seminar.

checks.label: Gives the model a role
checks.hint: Start with a role, e.g. 'You are a patient seminar tutor'.

checks.label: Says who it is for / your level
checks.hint: Say who the answer is for and their level.

checks.label: Asks for a specific output
checks.hint: Name the output: e.g. five bullet points and two discussion questions.

checks.label: Long enough to carry context
checks.hint: Aim for at least 18 words so context fits.

exercises.model_answer_tip: A strong version: 'You are a seminar tutor. I am a second-year history student with 30 minutes. Summarise the attached article in five bullets, then give two questions I could raise.'

exercises.title: Explain a concept
exercises.scenario: You do not understand 'opportunity cost' from your economics lecture.
exercises.task: Write a prompt that gets an explanation pitched at your level with an example.

checks.label: Sets a role
checks.hint: Give the model a role such as a tutor.

exercises.model_answer_tip: 'You are an economics tutor. I am a first-year with no background. Explain opportunity cost in under 150 words with one everyday example.'

exercises.title: Plan a study week
exercises.scenario: Exams start in 10 days. You have 4 modules and 2 hours a day.
exercises.task: Write a prompt that produces a usable revision plan.

checks.label: Gives constraints (time)
checks.hint: Include the days and hours you have.

checks.label: Mentions the modules/subjects
checks.hint: Say how many modules or which ones.

checks.label: Asks for a format
checks.hint: Ask for a timetable or table.

exercises.model_answer_tip: 'Make a day-by-day table for the next 10 days. I have 4 modules and 2 hours a day, and I am weakest in statistics, so give it extra time.'
